prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In this top-down close-up scene looking down at the camera wearer's lap (0.4–0.6 m away) and the floor beyond (0.8–1.0 m away), the depth map clearly separates the foreground limbs from the background floor and lap where patterned fabric and dark henna textures visually blend in RGB. A second person's henna-patterned left forearm extends horizontally from left to right across the centre at roughly 0.3–0.5 m from the camera wearer, positioned directly above the lap and below the camera wearer's downward gaze, while the camera wearer's own left and right hands enter from the bottom-left and bottom-right edges at 0.25–0.35 m (within immediate arm's reach, <0.5 m, and <0.1 m from the extended forearm). Both people's heads and torsos are out of view so neither person's face or gaze direction toward the camera wearer is visible, though the limb geometry indicates the camera wearer faces downward toward the arm. Across frames 1 to 5, the extended forearm and hand become progressively darker (retreating from roughly 0.3 m to 0.5 m as the hand's spread fingers enter full view on the right in frames 4–5), and in frame 5 the camera wearer's bright left hand reaches up and across to occlude the left portion of the extended forearm. The depth map is unreliable for small floor objects—such as the smartphone at the top right and the henna cone at the top left (~0.8 m away, still within full arm's reach)—which flatten into the dark background floor, as well as the white cotton wad above the arm which merges into the lap contour.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to parse the close-range workspace (all within 0.25–1.0 m and inside arm's reach of the camera wearer and the other person), detecting the smartphone on the floor at the top right (~0.8 m away, 0.3–0.4 m below the extended arm) as 'cell phone' in frames 1 and 2 before it leaves the frame or gets occluded by the spreading fingers in frames 3–5. It groups segments of the camera wearer's lower hands (0.25–0.35 m away at the bottom), the patterned lap (0.4–0.6 m away in the middle), a red garment on the upper left, and the other person's extended forearm (0.3–0.5 m away across the centre) into overlapping 'person' masks, without providing any head or gaze cues since all faces are out of view. Unlike the RGB image, the map explicitly isolates the distinct instance boundaries between the lower left and lower right hands in frame 3 and separates the overlapping vertical left arm from the horizontal extended forearm in frame 5. However, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence: in frames 1–3 the tattooed forearm and patterned skirt are largely missed (left black) due to heavy henna and fabric textures, in frame 4 they merge into a single undifferentiated pink 'person' blob, and in frame 5 the tattooed right-pointing hand is misclassified as 'bird' while a background person's feet/hands at the top right (~0.9 m away) are mislabelled as 'umbrella'. Small within-reach objects like the white cotton balls and the henna cones on the floor and in the right hand are completely undetected.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames because both the camera wearer's torso/head and the other person's torso/head are outside the close-up downward field of view, leaving no full-body landmarks to determine body facing or whether anyone looks toward the camera wearer. Only in frame 5 does a single magenta hand skeleton appear on the right side (~0.5 m from the camera wearer), accurately localizing the 2D joint positions and five spread fingers of the other person's extended left hand pointing to the right above the camera wearer's lap. This skeleton makes the exact finger articulation and palm orientation of the tattooed hand easier to read than in RGB where dark henna patterns obscure skin creases. However, the pose map is severely unreliable for the rest of the scene, completely failing to detect the same extended forearm and hand when its fingers are partially cropped on the right in frames 1–4. It also misses both of the camera wearer's own hands in the bottom foreground (0.25–0.35 m away, touching the forearm in frames 1–3, holding cotton in frame 4, and reaching across to occlude the forearm on the left while holding a cone on the right in frame 5) as well as another person's hands near the floor at the top of frame 5 (~0.9 m away).
